# moorage 0.0.1 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/moorage/0.0.1

# moorage

Install your self-authored agent **skills and plugins** into one central home, and
wire every agent harness to them from a single source of truth. A small Rust CLI.

*(Renamed from  skilldock, which collided on GitHub.)*

## Commands

```
moorage install   SOURCE [--mode dev|normal] [--skills a,b] [--harnesses claude,pi,omp,codex]
                         [--force] [--dry-run] [--no-post-install]
moorage uninstall NAME... [--dry-run]
moorage update    NAME... [--force] [--dry-run]
moorage list
moorage doctor    [--json]
```
All commands accept the six root overrides (see *Roots* below). `--dry-run` prints the
full action plan — skills, links, hook placements, registration merges, backups,
post_install — and mutates nothing.

## Skills (no manifest — behavior unchanged)

`SOURCE` may be a directory containing `SKILL.md` (single skill) or a repo with
`skills/*/SKILL.md` (multi-skill; scanned one level). The skill **name** comes from
the `SKILL.md` frontmatter `name:` and must be lowercase `[a-z0-9-]`, ≤ 64 chars,
with a non-empty `description:` (pi's discovery rule — enforced so the link name is
correct). A `skills/*` layout is **preferred** over a repo-root `SKILL.md`, so a repo
carrying both installs its `skills/<name>` payloads (the baseline shape).

Each skill installs to `~/.moorage/skills/{name}`:

| Mode | `~/.moorage/skills/{name}`is | Use it when |
|---|---|---|
| `dev`(default) | a symlink to the repo payload | authoring / iterating |
| `normal`(alias:`local`) | a real copy (excludes `.git`,`__pycache__`) | pinned snapshot |

and the agent roots link into the home:

```
~/.agents/skills/{name}  --+                              +-- dev:    repo payload (live)
                           +-->  ~/.moorage/skills/{name} -+
~/.claude/skills/{name}  --+                              +-- normal: a copy in the home
```
oh-my-pi reads both locations; all agents dedupe by real path.

## Plugins (`moorage.toml` manifest)

A `moorage.toml` at the repo root (or passed directly as `SOURCE`) upgrades a repo to
a plugin. **Its absence changes nothing** — no-manifest repos keep the exact behavior
above.

```
 = "conversate"          # optional plugin label (names placed hook files)
[]                    # optional preferences (see Precedence)
 = "dev"                 # dev | normal | local
 = ["claude", "pi", "omp", "codex"]
[[]]
 = "."                   # payload dir, repo-root-relative ("." = repo root)
 = "normal"              # optional per-skill override
 = ["claude"]       # optional per-skill override
[[]]
 = "hooks/claude/settings-snippet.json"   # merged into <claude-root>/settings.json
[[]]
 = "hooks/pi/conv-turn-counter.ts"         # placed into <pi-root>/agent/extensions/
[[]]
 = "hooks/pi/conv-turn-counter.ts"         # placed into <omp-root>/hooks/{stage}/
 = "pre"                                    # default "pre" when omitted
[[]]
 = "hooks/codex/hooks.json"                # merged into <codex-root>/hooks.json
[]
 = ["python scripts/example.py init"]         # optional; cwd = canonical skill dir
```
### Preference precedence

`CLI flags > per-skill entry > [install] table > built-in defaults` (mode `dev`, all
four harnesses). `--mode` / `--harnesses` on the command line mean "override the
manifest". The `harnesses` list gates both the skill links (`claude` → claude-root
link; any of `pi`/`omp`/`codex` → agents-root link) and the hook wiring per harness.
Per-skill `harnesses` gate that skill's links; plugin-level hooks follow
`CLI > [install] > default`.

### Hook FILES (pi, omp)

Placed as **file symlinks** named `moorage-{label}-{basename}` (label = manifest
`name`, else the first skill's name) pointing at the canonical copy inside
`~/.moorage/skills/{name}/...` — so dev/normal switching is transparent. If file
symlinks are unavailable (Windows without Developer Mode) the file is **copied** with
a loud warning, and doctor tracks drift of copied placements. Junctions are dir-only
and hardlinks die across volumes, so neither is used for files. Hook scripts must
live inside a `[[skills]]` payload (otherwise no canonical home copy exists — the
install refuses that hook).

### Registration MERGES (claude, codex)

The snippet's `hooks` block merges into the target config via a serde_json
round-trip that preserves unrelated keys:

- claude → `<claude-root>/settings.json`
- codex → `<codex-root>/hooks.json`(plus a printed reminder that codex loads hooks only with`[features] hooks = true`in`~/.codex/config.toml`— moorage**never**edits that file)

Merges are **append-if-absent** (exact-equality dedupe ⇒ idempotent re-installs), and
a syntactically invalid target config is refused, never clobbered. Before the
**first** modification of each config, a `.bak` copy goes into `~/.moorage/backups/`
(named `{basename}.{epoch}.bak`, recorded in state).

**Command-path rewriting** (design ruling; the v2 exact rule is unrecovered): every
whitespace-separated token of a `command` / `commandWindows` string that resolves —
relative to an installed skill payload root — to an existing file is rewritten to the
absolute path of that file under the canonical home
(`~/.moorage/skills/{name}/...`). The **home** path, never the source repo path, so
dev-mode symlinks keep the loop live. Rewritten paths containing spaces are quoted; a
token that itself contains spaces can never match (whitespace split — a known v2
limitation). Snippets should therefore reference their scripts by payload-relative
paths (e.g. `hooks/claude/counter.ps1`).

### Reversibility

Every inserted JSON entry is persisted **verbatim** in `state.toml` *and* is
self-marked by containing the `~/.moorage/skills/{name}` path in its command (no
marker keys are injected — that would fight harness schema validation). `uninstall`:

- unmerges exactly the recorded entries (falling back to the home-path marker for
entries a user edited in place); emptied configs are left as `{}`, never deleted;
- removes placed hook files and agent links (links are dropped, targets untouched);
- removes the home entry — for dev mode the **symlink only**, never the target repo;
- deletes the state record.

Source repositories are never touched. Legacy state records (pre-plugin, five fields)
still load; uninstalling one derives the two conventional agent-link paths and
deletes each **only after verifying it actually points into the moorage home** —
anything else is skipped with a warning.

### post_install

Commands run after all components are placed, with `cwd` = the canonical skill dir in
the home (first skill for multi-skill plugins). Each command is echoed and its
outcome recorded in state. `--no-post-install` skips them (recorded as `skipped`). A
failing command **reports loudly, marks the state record ( failed(N)), sets exit
code 1, and does NOT roll back the install** (design ruling — fix the cause and
re-run, or uninstall).

`update` never runs post_install.## update

- **dev**installs: verify and repair the whole chain — home link, agent links, hook files; re-apply merges when snippets changed (stale recorded entries are unmerged, new ones merged; stale hook files removed).
- **normal**installs: hash-compare (in-crate FNV-1a-64 over the payload tree) and re-copy- **only if the source changed**;- **refuse**when the installed copy was hand-edited (or when a legacy record has no stored hash to verify against) —- `--force`overrides.

## doctor

Read-only, always. Checks: state.toml parse health; full chain integrity (agent link
→ home → payload); dangling/re-targeted links; placed hook files (missing, dangling,
copy drift vs canonical); merged registrations (recorded entries still present,
target configs valid); **orphaned** moorage-marked entries (home path in the command
but absent from state); unmanaged entries (reported, never touched) incl. pi
name-rule violations; shadowing (same name under claude-root and agents-root
resolving to different real paths); normal-mode content drift vs source; dev-mode git
hygiene (dirty tree, non-main branch — best effort); manifest preference drift
(manifest prefers a different mode than installed); `AGENTS.md` inside a skill dir
(pi issue #2473). `--json` emits the findings machine-readably. Exit code is 0 even
with findings; nonzero means doctor itself failed to run.

## Conflicts, idempotency, dry-run

- An entry already resolving to the right target is left alone (idempotent re-runs); merges dedupe by exact equality.
- A conflicting foreign entry is **refused**with a clear message;`--force`renames it to a sibling`{name}.bak-N`and replaces it.
- `--dry-run`prints the full plan and changes nothing (configs are only read).

## Roots (for tests / alternate setups)

Flag > env > default, uniformly:

| Setting | Flag | Env | Default | Used for |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| home | `--home` | `MOORAGE_HOME` | `~/.moorage` | canonical home, state, backups |
| agents root | `--agents-root` | `MOORAGE_AGENTS_ROOT` | `~/.agents` | pi/omp/codex skill links |
| claude root | `--claude-root` | `MOORAGE_CLAUDE_ROOT` | `~/.claude` | Claude skill links + `settings.json`merges |
| pi root | `--pi-root` | `MOORAGE_PI_ROOT` | `~/.pi` | hook files under `agent/extensions/` |
| omp root | `--omp-root` | `MOORAGE_OMP_ROOT` | `~/.omp` | hook files under `hooks/{stage}/` |
| codex root | `--codex-root` | `MOORAGE_CODEX_ROOT` | `~/.codex` | `hooks.json`merges |

## state.toml

`~/.moorage/state.toml` records, per skill: `name`, `mode`, `source`, `installed`/
`updated` (epoch secs), and — for plugin installs — `plugin` label, `manifest` path,
effective `harnesses`, `home_kind` (symlink/junction/copy), `copy_hash` (normal
mode), `[[links]]` (path/kind/target), `[[hook_files]]` (path/kind/target),
`[[merges]]` (file/event/verbatim entry), `[[post_install]]` (command/status), and
`[[backups]]` (original/backup). Legacy five-field records load unchanged.

## Windows link fallback

Directory links try: real symlink (needs Developer Mode or elevation) → NTFS
**junction** via `cmd /c mklink /J` (no privileges) → **copy** with a loud warning.
File placements try: file symlink → copy (drift tracked by doctor). On non-Windows,
symlinks are used directly.

## Unverified upstream paths (honesty notes)

- **omp**: upstream documents only- *project-level*- `.omp/hooks/{stage}/*.ts`discovery. The user-level- `<omp-root>/hooks/{stage}/`placement is a- **best-documented-guess**(unverified upstream). doctor emits a- `warn`note when omp hook files are installed; override with- `--omp-root`.
- **codex**: whether codex reads a- *user-level*- `hooks.json`at all is- **unverified**(only project-level- `.codex/hooks.json`is documented). doctor emits a- `warn`note when codex merges are installed; override with- `--codex-root`.
- **pi**(- `~/.pi/agent/extensions`) and- **claude**(- `~/.claude/settings.json`) are documented/known paths.

## Design rulings (unrecovered v2 details, decided here)

- **Command rewriting token rule**: whitespace token → resolve against installed payload roots (manifest order, first match) → rewrite to the absolute canonical home path; quote only when the result contains spaces; absolute tokens skipped.
- **Mode name**: the CLI keeps- `dev|normal`;- `local`(the v2 name) is accepted as an alias both on the CLI and in manifests.
- **omp**:- `stage`default- `"pre"`(the only value ever observed).
- **post_install failure**: loud warning +- `failed(N)`in state + exit 1, no rollback;- `--no-post-install`records- `skipped`;- `update`never runs post_install.
- `--force`backups- `{name}.bak-N`convention (the pinned minimal-Rust behavior) instead of moving into- `~/.moorage/backups/`; the backups dir holds config- `.bak`snapshots only, named- `{basename}.{epoch}.bak`.
- **backups/ contents are permanent**: uninstall does not delete taken backups (traceability).
- **Multi-skill plugins**: post_install cwd = first skill's canonical dir; hook artifacts are named after the manifest- `name`(else the first skill); the plugin component ledger (hook files, merges, post_install, backups) rides on the first skill's state record.
- **Manifests must declare**: a manifest with no skills entry is an error (hooks need a payload to live in).- `[[skills]]`
- **Corrupt state.toml**: mutating commands refuse to run over an unparseable ledger (protecting the live records); doctor reports it as a- `fail`finding.
- `update`flags- `--force`(attested) plus- `--dry-run`(inferred-carried).
- **Content hashing**: in-crate FNV-1a-64 (stable across releases, zero deps) — std's- `DefaultHasher`is explicitly not used for persisted hashes.

## Build

```
cargo build --release          # binary at target/release/moorage(.exe)
cargo install --path .         # optional: install to ~/.cargo/bin
```
Tests: `cargo test` (unit: manifest parse, merge/unmerge/rewrite, state round-trip
incl. legacy records) and `python -m pytest tests/ -q` (29 black-box tests against
the built binary with all six roots pinned to temp dirs; set `MOORAGE_BIN` to point
at a specific exe, else `target/debug/moorage`).

Requires a stable Rust toolchain. Dependencies: `clap` (CLI), `serde` + `toml`
(manifests + state), `serde_json` (registration merges).

# polkadot_jemalloc_shim - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/polkadot-jemalloc-shim/0.6.0/polkadot_jemalloc_shim/

## Expand description

Shim crate to enable `jemalloc-allocator` feature for Polkadot crates.

Because [there doesn’t exist any easier way right now](https://github.com/rust-lang/cargo/issues/1197), we
need an entire crate to handle `jemalloc` enabling/disabling. This way we can enable it by
default on Linux, but have it optional on all other OSes.

# sim_lib_sound_core - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sim-lib-sound-core/0.1.0-rc.1/sim_lib_sound_core/

## Expand description

Core sound primitives for the SIM music constellation.

This crate defines the foundational acoustic types shared by the
sound/synthesis layer: [ Frequency](https://docs.rs/struct.Frequency.html),

[, and](https://docs.rs/struct.Amplitude.html)

`Amplitude`[quantities; the](https://docs.rs/struct.Phase.html)

`Phase`[,](https://docs.rs/struct.Partial.html)

`Partial`[, and](https://docs.rs/struct.Envelope.html)

`Envelope`[models that build a spectral tone from sinusoidal components; and helpers for default envelopes and equal-temperament pitch-to-frequency conversion.](https://docs.rs/struct.Tone.html)

`Tone`## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Amplitude](https://docs.rs/struct.Amplitude.html)
- A non-negative linear amplitude.
- [Envelope](https://docs.rs/struct.Envelope.html)
- An attack/decay/sustain/release amplitude envelope.
- [Frequency](https://docs.rs/struct.Frequency.html)
- A positive frequency in hertz.
- [Partial](https://docs.rs/struct.Partial.html)
- A single sinusoidal component of a tone.
- [Phase](https://docs.rs/struct.Phase.html)
- A phase angle in radians.
- [Tone](https://docs.rs/struct.Tone.html)
- A complete tone: a set of `Partial``Envelope`

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Envelope](https://docs.rs/enum.EnvelopeShape.html)- Shape
- The interpolation curve applied across an `Envelope`
- [Sound](https://docs.rs/enum.SoundCoreError.html)- Core - Error
- Error raised when sound primitives are constructed with invalid values.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [default_](https://docs.rs/fn.default_envelope.html)- envelope
- Returns a general-purpose default envelope (short attack and decay, high sustain, moderate release, linear shape).
- [equal_](https://docs.rs/fn.equal_temperament_frequency.html)- temperament_ - frequency
- Returns the 12-tone equal-temperament frequency of `pitch`, with A4 (MIDI 69) anchored at 440 Hz.

# chameleon - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/chameleon-pq/0.4.0/chameleon/

Skip to main content Crate chameleon  Copy item path  Source  `pub use error::`ChameleonError ;`pub use error::`Result ;aead Pluggable AEAD-laag voor het datapad. config TOML-configuratie en CLI voor Chameleon-PQ. crypto Cryptografische kern: pluggable peer-authenticatie (Authenticator-trait),
het handshake-transcript, en key-derivation helpers. engine De crypto-engine: het ENE punt waar uitgaand verkeer wordt versleuteld. error frame Wire-frame voor het DATApad (blijft onder de MTU). hsobf Statische-sleutel obfuscatie voor de HANDSHAKE-envelope (Fase 2). net Netwerk-glue: UDP-socket loops die de handshake en het datapad bedraden. obf Obfuscatie-laag voor het DATApad: QUIC-stijl header-protection + padding. pacer Constant-rate pacer (Fase 3): timing-/cover-traffic-obfuscatie. rekey Rekey-driver die het gedeelde-socket-probleem oplost. session Actieve sessie: per-richting sleutels, nonce-beheer, AEAD via ring,
sliding-window replay-bescherming, en een SessionManager voor rekey. tun_iface  TUN-interface laag: cross-platform, asynchroon. tunnel Handshake: 2048-byte gepadde berichten met één gedeeld KEM-slot,
fragmentatie voor MTU-veilig transport, en de state machine met
transcript-ondertekening (Ed25519 via de Authenticator-trait). udp Gebatchte UDP-I/O via `quinn-udp` (GSO op verzenden, GRO op ontvangen), met
graceful per-pakket fallback op oude kernels / niet-Linux.

# sp_trie - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/sp-trie/46.0.0/target-redirect/sp_trie/

## Expand description

Utility functions to interact with Substrate’s Base-16 Modified Merkle Patricia tree (“trie”).

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [accessed_](https://docs.rs/accessed_nodes_tracker/index.html)- nodes_ - tracker
- Helpers for checking for duplicate nodes.
- [cache](https://docs.rs/cache/index.html)
- Trie Cache
- [nibble_](https://docs.rs/nibble_ops/index.html)- ops
- Various re-exports from the `trie-db`crate. Utility methods to work on radix 16 nibble.
- [proof_](https://docs.rs/proof_size_extension/index.html)- size_ - extension
- Externalities extension that provides access to the current proof size of the underlying recorder.
- [recorder](https://docs.rs/recorder/index.html)
- Trie recorder
- [recorder_](https://docs.rs/recorder_ext/index.html)- ext
- Extension for the default recorder.
- [trie_](https://docs.rs/trie_types/index.html)- types
- This module is for non generic definition of trie type.
Only the `Hasher`trait is generic in this case.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Compact](https://docs.rs/struct.CompactProof.html)- Proof
- Storage proof in compact form.
- [HashKey](https://docs.rs/struct.HashKey.html)
- Various re-exports from the `memory-db`crate. Key function that only uses the hash
- [KeySpacedDB](https://docs.rs/struct.KeySpacedDB.html)
- `HashDB`implementation that append a encoded prefix (unique id bytes) in addition to the prefix of every key value.
- [KeySpacedDB](https://docs.rs/struct.KeySpacedDBMut.html)- Mut
- `HashDBMut`implementation that append a encoded prefix (unique id bytes) in addition to the prefix of every key value.
- [Layout](https://docs.rs/struct.LayoutV0.html)- V0
- substrate trie layout
- [Layout](https://docs.rs/struct.LayoutV1.html)- V1
- substrate trie layout, with external value nodes.
- [Node](https://docs.rs/struct.NodeCodec.html)- Codec
- The Substrate format implementation of `NodeCodec`. Concrete implementation of a`NodeCodecT`
- [Prefixed](https://docs.rs/struct.PrefixedKey.html)- Key
- Various re-exports from the `memory-db`crate. Key function that concatenates prefix and hash.
- [Random](https://docs.rs/struct.RandomState.html)- State
- `RandomState`is the default state for- `HashMap`
- [Recorder](https://docs.rs/struct.Recorder.html)
- Various re-exports from the `trie-db`crate. Records trie nodes as they pass it.
- [Storage](https://docs.rs/struct.StorageProof.html)- Proof
- A proof that some set of key-value pairs are included in the storage trie. The proof contains the storage values so that the partial storage backend can be reconstructed by a verifier that does not already have access to the key-value pairs.
- [TrieDB](https://docs.rs/struct.TrieDBDoubleEndedIterator.html)- Double - Ended - Iterator
- Various re-exports from the `trie-db`crate. Double ended iterator for going through all values in the trie in pre-order traversal order.
- [TrieDB](https://docs.rs/struct.TrieDBIterator.html)- Iterator
- Various re-exports from the `trie-db`crate. Iterator for going through all values in the trie in pre-order traversal order.
- [TrieDB](https://docs.rs/struct.TrieDBKeyDoubleEndedIterator.html)- KeyDouble - Ended - Iterator
- Various re-exports from the `trie-db`crate. Double ended iterator for going through all of key with values in the trie in pre-order traversal order.
- [TrieDB](https://docs.rs/struct.TrieDBKeyIterator.html)- KeyIterator
- Various re-exports from the `trie-db`crate. Iterator for going through all of key with values in the trie in pre-order traversal order.
- [TrieDB](https://docs.rs/struct.TrieDBNodeDoubleEndedIterator.html)- Node - Double - Ended - Iterator
- Various re-exports from the `trie-db`crate. Double ended iterator for going through all nodes in the trie in pre-order traversal order.
- [TrieDB](https://docs.rs/struct.TrieDBRawIterator.html)- RawIterator
- Various re-exports from the `trie-db`crate. Iterator for going through all nodes in the trie in pre-order traversal order.
- [Trie](https://docs.rs/struct.TrieStream.html)- Stream
- The Substrate format implementation of `TrieStream`. Codec-flavored TrieStream.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Compact](https://docs.rs/enum.CompactProofError.html)- Proof - Error
- Trie codec reexport, mainly child trie support for trie compact proof. Error for trie node decoding.
- [Error](https://docs.rs/enum.Error.html)
- Our `NodeCodec`-specific error. Error type used for trie related errors.
- [Merkle](https://docs.rs/enum.MerkleValue.html)- Value
- Either the `hash`or`value`of a node depending on its size.
- [Node](https://docs.rs/enum.NodePlan.html)- Plan
- Various re-exports from the `trie-db`crate. A`NodePlan`is a blueprint for decoding a node from a byte slice. The`NodePlan`is created by parsing an encoded node and can be reused multiple times. This is useful as a`Node`borrows from a byte slice and this struct does not.
- [Storage](https://docs.rs/enum.StorageProofError.html)- Proof - Error
- Error associated with the `storage_proof`module.
- [Value](https://docs.rs/enum.ValuePlan.html)- Plan
- Various re-exports from the `trie-db`crate. Plan for value representation in`NodePlan`.
- [Verify](https://docs.rs/enum.VerifyError.html)- Error
- Errors that may occur during proof verification. Most of the errors types simply indicate that the proof is invalid with respect to the statement being verified, and the exact error type can be used for debugging.

## Statics[§](https://docs.rs#statics)

- [EMPTY_](https://docs.rs/static.EMPTY_PREFIX.html)- PREFIX
- Various re-exports from the `hash-db`crate. An empty prefix constant. Can be use when the prefix is not use internally or for root nodes.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [AsHashDB](https://docs.rs/trait.AsHashDB.html)
- Reexport from `hash_db`, with genericity set for`Hasher`trait.
- [HashDBT](https://docs.rs/trait.HashDBT.html)
- Various re-exports from the `hash-db`crate. Trait modelling datastore keyed by a hash defined by the`Hasher`.
- [KeyFunction](https://docs.rs/trait.KeyFunction.html)
- Various re-exports from the `memory-db`crate.
- [Proof](https://docs.rs/trait.ProofSizeProvider.html)- Size - Provider
- Type that is able to provide a proof size estimation.
- [Query](https://docs.rs/trait.Query.html)
- Various re-exports from the `trie-db`crate. Description of what kind of query will be made to the trie.
- [Trie](https://docs.rs/trait.Trie.html)
- Various re-exports from the `trie-db`crate. A key-value datastore implemented as a database-backed modified Merkle tree.
- [Trie](https://docs.rs/trait.TrieCache.html)- Cache
- Various re-exports from the `trie-db`crate. A cache that can be used to speed-up certain operations when accessing the trie.
- [Trie](https://docs.rs/trait.TrieConfiguration.html)- Configuration
- Various re-exports from the `trie-db`crate. This trait associates a trie definition with preferred methods. It also contains own default implementations and can be used to allow switching implementation.
- [Trie](https://docs.rs/trait.TrieLayout.html)- Layout
- Various re-exports from the `trie-db`crate. Trait with definition of trie layout. Contains all associated trait needed for a trie definition or implementation.
- [TrieMut](https://docs.rs/trait.TrieMut.html)
- Various re-exports from the `trie-db`crate. A key-value datastore implemented as a database-backed modified Merkle tree.
- [Trie](https://docs.rs/trait.TrieRecorder.html)- Recorder
- Various re-exports from the `trie-db`crate. A trie recorder that can be used to record all kind of`TrieAccess`
- [Trie](https://docs.rs/trait.TrieRecorderProvider.html)- Recorder - Provider
- Type that is able to provide a `trie_db::TrieRecorder`

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [child_](https://docs.rs/fn.child_delta_trie_root.html)- delta_ - trie_ - root
- Determine a child trie root given a hash DB and delta values. H is the default hasher, but a generic implementation may ignore this type parameter and use other hashers.
- [child_](https://docs.rs/fn.child_trie_root.html)- trie_ - root
- Determine a child trie root given its ordered contents, closed form. H is the default hasher, but a generic implementation may ignore this type parameter and use other hashers.
- [decode_](https://docs.rs/fn.decode_compact.html)- compact
- Trie codec reexport, mainly child trie support for trie compact proof. Decode a compact proof.
- [delta_](https://docs.rs/fn.delta_trie_root.html)- trie_ - root
- Determine a trie root given a hash DB and delta values.
- [empty_](https://docs.rs/fn.empty_child_trie_root.html)- child_ - trie_ - root
- Determine the empty child trie root.
- [empty_](https://docs.rs/fn.empty_trie_root.html)- trie_ - root
- Determine the empty trie root.
- [encode_](https://docs.rs/fn.encode_compact.html)- compact
- Trie codec reexport, mainly child trie support for trie compact proof. Encode a compact proof.
- [generate_](https://docs.rs/fn.generate_trie_proof.html)- trie_ - proof
- Create a proof for a subset of keys in a trie.
- [prefixed_](https://docs.rs/fn.prefixed_key.html)- key
- Various re-exports from the `memory-db`crate. Derive a database key from hash value of the node (key) and the node prefix.
- [read_](https://docs.rs/fn.read_child_trie_first_descendant_value.html)- child_ - trie_ - first_ - descendant_ - value
- Read the `trie_db::MerkleValue`
- [read_](https://docs.rs/fn.read_child_trie_hash.html)- child_ - trie_ - hash
- Read a hash from the child trie.
- [read_](https://docs.rs/fn.read_child_trie_value.html)- child_ - trie_ - value
- Read a value from the child trie.
- [read_](https://docs.rs/fn.read_child_trie_value_with.html)- child_ - trie_ - value_ - with
- Read a value from the child trie with given query.
- [read_](https://docs.rs/fn.read_trie_first_descendant_value.html)- trie_ - first_ - descendant_ - value
- Read the `trie_db::MerkleValue`
- [read_](https://docs.rs/fn.read_trie_value.html)- trie_ - value
- Read a value from the trie.
- [read_](https://docs.rs/fn.read_trie_value_with.html)- trie_ - value_ - with
- Read a value from the trie with given Query.
- [verify_](https://docs.rs/fn.verify_trie_proof.html)- trie_ - proof
- Verify a set of key-value pairs against a trie root and a proof.

## Type Aliases[§](https://docs.rs#types)

- [CError](https://docs.rs/type.CError.html)
- Various re-exports from the `trie-db`crate. Alias accessor to`NodeCodec`associated`Error`type from a`TrieLayout`.
- [DBValue](https://docs.rs/type.DBValue.html)
- Various re-exports from the `trie-db`crate. Database value
- [Generic](https://docs.rs/type.GenericMemoryDB.html)- MemoryDB
- Reexport from `hash_db`, with genericity set for`Hasher`trait.
- [HashDB](https://docs.rs/type.HashDB.html)
- Reexport from `hash_db`, with genericity set for`Hasher`trait.
- [Lookup](https://docs.rs/type.Lookup.html)
- Querying interface, as in `trie_db`but less generic.
- [MemoryDB](https://docs.rs/type.MemoryDB.html)
- Reexport from `hash_db`, with genericity set for`Hasher`trait. This uses a noops`KeyFunction`(key addressing must be hashed or using an encoding scheme that avoid key conflict).
- [Prefixed](https://docs.rs/type.PrefixedMemoryDB.html)- MemoryDB
- Reexport from `hash_db`, with genericity set for`Hasher`trait. This uses a`KeyFunction`for prefixing keys internally (avoiding key conflict for non random keys).
- [RawStorage](https://docs.rs/type.RawStorageProof.html)- Proof
- Raw storage proof type (just raw trie nodes).
- [TrieDB](https://docs.rs/type.TrieDB.html)
- Persistent trie database read-access interface for a given hasher.
- [TrieDB](https://docs.rs/type.TrieDBBuilder.html)- Builder
- Builder for creating a `TrieDB`
- [TrieDB](https://docs.rs/type.TrieDBMut.html)- Mut
- Persistent trie database write-access interface for a given hasher.
- [TrieDB](https://docs.rs/type.TrieDBMutBuilder.html)- MutBuilder
- Builder for creating a `TrieDBMut`
- [Trie](https://docs.rs/type.TrieError.html)- Error
- TrieDB error over `TrieConfiguration`trait.
- [Trie](https://docs.rs/type.TrieHash.html)- Hash
- Hash type for a trie layout.

## Type Aliases[§](https://docs.rs#types)

- [DBValue](https://docs.rs/type.DBValue.html)
- Various re-exports from the `trie-db`crate. Database value
- [Generic](https://docs.rs/type.GenericMemoryDB.html)- MemoryDB
- Reexport from `hash_db`, with genericity set for`Hasher`trait.
- [HashDB](https://docs.rs/type.HashDB.html)
- Reexport from `hash_db`, with genericity set for`Hasher`trait.
- [Lookup](https://docs.rs/type.Lookup.html)
- Querying interface, as in `trie_db`but less generic.
- [MemoryDB](https://docs.rs/type.MemoryDB.html)
- Reexport from `hash_db`, with genericity set for`Hasher`trait. This uses a noops`KeyFunction`(key addressing must be hashed or using an encoding scheme that avoid key conflict).
- [Prefixed](https://docs.rs/type.PrefixedMemoryDB.html)- MemoryDB
- Reexport from `hash_db`, with genericity set for`Hasher`trait. This uses a`KeyFunction`for prefixing keys internally (avoiding key conflict for non random keys).
- [RawStorage](https://docs.rs/type.RawStorageProof.html)- Proof
- Raw storage proof type (just raw trie nodes).
- [TrieDB](https://docs.rs/type.TrieDB.html)
- Persistent trie database read-access interface for a given hasher.
- [TrieDB](https://docs.rs/type.TrieDBBuilder.html)- Builder
- Builder for creating a `TrieDB`
- [TrieDB](https://docs.rs/type.TrieDBMut.html)- Mut
- Persistent trie database write-access interface for a given hasher.
- [TrieDB](https://docs.rs/type.TrieDBMutBuilder.html)- MutBuilder
- Builder for creating a `TrieDBMut`
- [Trie](https://docs.rs/type.TrieError.html)- Error
- TrieDB error over `TrieConfiguration`trait.
- [Trie](https://docs.rs/type.TrieHash.html)- Hash
- Hash type for a trie layout.

---

[319](#319)
[320](#320)pub fn delta_trie_root<L: TrieConfiguration, I, A, B, DB, V>(
[322](#322)	db: &mut DB,
[323](#323)	mut root: TrieHash<L>,
[324](#324)	delta: I,
[325](#325)	recorder: Option<&mut dyn trie_db::TrieRecorder<TrieHash<L>>>,
[326](#326)	cache: Option<&mut dyn TrieCache<L::Codec>>,
[327](#327)) -> Result<TrieHash<L>, Box<TrieError<L>>>
[328](#328)where
[329](#329)	I: IntoIterator<Item = (A, B)>,
[330](#330)	A: Borrow<[u8]>,
[331](#331)	B: Borrow<Option<V>>,
[332](#332)	V: Borrow<[u8]>,
[333](#333)	DB: hash_db::HashDB<L::Hash, trie_db::DBValue>,
[334](#334){
[335](#335)	{
[336](#336)		let mut trie = TrieDBMutBuilder::<L>::from_existing(db, &mut root)
[337](#337)			.with_optional_cache(cache)
[338](#338)			.with_optional_recorder(recorder)
[339](#339)			.build();
[340](#340)
[341](#341)		let mut delta = delta.into_iter().collect::<Vec<_>>();
[342](#342)		delta.sort_by(|l, r| l.0.borrow().cmp(r.0.borrow()));
[343](#343)
[344](#344)		for (key, change) in delta {
[345](#345)			match change.borrow() {
[346](#346)				Some(val) => trie.insert(key.borrow(), val.borrow())?,
[347](#347)				None => trie.remove(key.borrow())?,
[348](#348)			};
[349](#349)		}
[350](#350)	}

[536](#536)pub struct KeySpacedDB<'a, DB: ?Sized, H>(&'a DB, &'a [u8], PhantomData<H>);
[539](#539)
[540](#540)pub struct KeySpacedDBMut<'a, DB: ?Sized, H>(&'a mut DB, &'a [u8], PhantomData<H>);
[545](#545)
[546](#546)fn keyspace_as_prefix_alloc(ks: &[u8], prefix: Prefix) -> (Vec<u8>, Option<u8>) {
[549](#549)	let mut result = vec![0; ks.len() + prefix.0.len()];
[550](#550)	result[..ks.len()].copy_from_slice(ks);
[551](#551)	result[ks.len()..].copy_from_slice(prefix.0);
[552](#552)	(result, prefix.1)
[553](#553)}
[554](#554)

[634](#634)mod trie_constants {
[636](#636)	const FIRST_PREFIX: u8 = 0b_00 << 6;
[637](#637)	pub const LEAF_PREFIX_MASK: u8 = 0b_01 << 6;
[638](#638)	pub const BRANCH_WITHOUT_MASK: u8 = 0b_10 << 6;
[639](#639)	pub const BRANCH_WITH_MASK: u8 = 0b_11 << 6;
[640](#640)	pub const EMPTY_TRIE: u8 = FIRST_PREFIX | (0b_00 << 4);
[641](#641)	pub const ALT_HASHING_LEAF_PREFIX_MASK: u8 = FIRST_PREFIX | (0b_1 << 5);
[642](#642)	pub const ALT_HASHING_BRANCH_WITH_MASK: u8 = FIRST_PREFIX | (0b_01 << 4);
[643](#643)	pub const ESCAPE_COMPACT_HEADER: u8 = EMPTY_TRIE | 0b_00_01;

[660](#660)	pub fn create_trie<L: TrieLayout>(
[661](#661)		data: &[(&[u8], &[u8])],
[662](#662)	) -> (MemoryDB<L::Hash>, trie_db::TrieHash<L>) {
[663](#663)		let mut db = MemoryDB::default();
[664](#664)		let mut root = Default::default();
[665](#665)
[666](#666)		{
[667](#667)			let mut trie = trie_db::TrieDBMutBuilder::<L>::new(&mut db, &mut root).build();
[668](#668)			for (k, v) in data {
[669](#669)				trie.insert(k, v).expect("Inserts data");
[670](#670)			}
[671](#671)		}
[672](#672)
[673](#673)		let mut recorder = Recorder::<L>::new();
[674](#674)		{
[675](#675)			let trie = trie_db::TrieDBBuilder::<L>::new(&mut db, &mut root)
[676](#676)				.with_recorder(&mut recorder)
[677](#677)				.build();
[678](#678)			for (k, _v) in data {
[679](#679)				trie.get(k).unwrap();
[680](#680)			}
[681](#681)		}
[682](#682)
[683](#683)		(db, root)

[708](#708)	fn check_equivalent<T: TrieConfiguration>(input: &Vec<(&[u8], &[u8])>) {
[709](#709)		{
[710](#710)			let closed_form = T::trie_root(input.clone());
[711](#711)			let d = T::trie_root_unhashed(input.clone());
[712](#712)			println!("Data: {:#x?}, {:#x?}", d, Blake2Hasher::hash(&d[..]));
[713](#713)			let persistent = {
[714](#714)				let mut memdb = MemoryDBMeta::default();
[715](#715)				let mut root = Default::default();
[716](#716)				let mut t = TrieDBMutBuilder::<T>::new(&mut memdb, &mut root).build();
[717](#717)				for (x, y) in input.iter().rev() {
[718](#718)					t.insert(x, y).unwrap();
[719](#719)				}
[720](#720)				*t.root()
[721](#721)			};
[722](#722)			assert_eq!(closed_form, persistent);
[723](#723)		}
[724](#724)	}
[725](#725)
[726](#726)	fn check_iteration<T: TrieConfiguration>(input: &Vec<(&[u8], &[u8])>) {
[727](#727)		let mut memdb = MemoryDBMeta::default();
[728](#728)		let mut root = Default::default();
[729](#729)		{
[730](#730)			let mut t = TrieDBMutBuilder::<T>::new(&mut memdb, &mut root).build();
[731](#731)			for (x, y) in input.clone() {
[732](#732)				t.insert(x, y).unwrap();
[733](#733)			}
[734](#734)		}
[735](#735)		{
[736](#736)			let t = TrieDBBuilder::<T>::new(&memdb, &root).build();
[737](#737)			assert_eq!(
[738](#738)				input.iter().map(|(i, j)| (i.to_vec(), j.to_vec())).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
[739](#739)				t.iter()
[740](#740)					.unwrap()
[741](#741)					.map(|x| x.map(|y| (y.0, y.1.to_vec())).unwrap())
[742](#742)					.collect::<Vec<_>>()
[743](#743)			);
[744](#744)		}
[745](#745)	}
[746](#746)
[747](#747)	fn check_input(input: &Vec<(&[u8], &[u8])>) {

[861](#861)	fn populate_trie<'db, T: TrieConfiguration>(
[862](#862)		db: &'db mut dyn HashDB<T::Hash, DBValue>,
[863](#863)		root: &'db mut TrieHash<T>,
[864](#864)		v: &[(Vec<u8>, Vec<u8>)],
[865](#865)	) -> TrieDBMut<'db, T> {
[866](#866)		let mut t = TrieDBMutBuilder::<T>::new(db, root).build();
[867](#867)		for i in 0..v.len() {
[868](#868)			let key: &[u8] = &v[i].0;
[869](#869)			let val: &[u8] = &v[i].1;
[870](#870)			t.insert(key, val).unwrap();
[871](#871)		}
[872](#872)		t
[873](#873)	}
[874](#874)
[875](#875)	fn unpopulate_trie<T: TrieConfiguration>(t: &mut TrieDBMut<'_, T>, v: &[(Vec<u8>, Vec<u8>)]) {
[876](#876)		for i in v {
[877](#877)			let key: &[u8] = &i.0;
[878](#878)			t.remove(key).unwrap();
[879](#879)		}
[880](#880)	}

[888](#888)		let mut seed = <Blake2Hasher as Hasher>::Out::zero();
[889](#889)		for test_i in 0..10_000 {
[890](#890)			if test_i % 50 == 0 {
[891](#891)				println!("{:?} of 10000 stress tests done", test_i);
[892](#892)			}
[893](#893)			let x = StandardMap {
[894](#894)				alphabet: Alphabet::Custom(b"@QWERTYUIOPASDFGHJKLZXCVBNM[/]^_".to_vec()),
[895](#895)				min_key: 5,
[896](#896)				journal_key: 0,
[897](#897)				value_mode: ValueMode::Index,
[898](#898)				count: 100,
[899](#899)			}
[900](#900)			.make_with(seed.as_fixed_bytes_mut());
[901](#901)
[902](#902)			let real = L::trie_root(x.clone());
[903](#903)			let mut memdb = MemoryDB::default();
[904](#904)			let mut root = Default::default();
[905](#905)
[906](#906)			let mut memtrie = populate_trie::<L>(&mut memdb, &mut root, &x);
[907](#907)
[908](#908)			memtrie.commit();
[909](#909)			if *memtrie.root() != real {
[910](#910)				println!("TRIE MISMATCH");
[911](#911)				println!();
[912](#912)				println!("{:?} vs {:?}", memtrie.root(), real);
[913](#913)				for i in &x {
[914](#914)					println!("{:#x?} -> {:#x?}", i.0, i.1);
[915](#915)				}
[916](#916)			}
[917](#917)			assert_eq!(*memtrie.root(), real);
[918](#918)			unpopulate_trie::<L>(&mut memtrie, &x);
[919](#919)			memtrie.commit();
[920](#920)			let hashed_null_node = hashed_null_node::<L>();
[921](#921)			if *memtrie.root() != hashed_null_node {
[922](#922)				println!("- TRIE MISMATCH");
[923](#923)				println!();
[924](#924)				println!("{:?} vs {:?}", memtrie.root(), hashed_null_node);
[925](#925)				for i in &x {
[926](#926)					println!("{:#x?} -> {:#x?}", i.0, i.1);
[927](#927)				}
[928](#928)			}
[929](#929)			assert_eq!(*memtrie.root(), hashed_null_node);
[930](#930)		}

# sp_trie::accessed_nodes_tracker - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sp-trie/46.0.0/sp_trie/accessed_nodes_tracker/index.html

## Expand description

Helpers for checking for duplicate nodes.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Accessed](https://docs.rs/struct.AccessedNodesTracker.html)- Nodes - Tracker
- Helper struct used to ensure that a storage proof doesn’t contain duplicate or unused nodes.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Error](https://docs.rs/enum.Error.html)
- Error associated with the `AccessedNodesTracker`module.

---

# sp_trie::cache - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sp-trie/46.0.0/sp_trie/cache/index.html

## Expand description

Trie Cache

Provides an implementation of the [ TrieCache](https://docs.rs/trait.TrieCache.html) trait.
The implementation is split into three types

[,](https://docs.rs/struct.SharedTrieCache.html)

`SharedTrieCache`[and](https://docs.rs/struct.LocalTrieCache.html)

`LocalTrieCache`[. The](https://docs.rs/struct.TrieCache.html)

`TrieCache`[is the instance that should be kept around for the entire lifetime of the node. It will store all cached trie nodes and values on a global level. Then there is the](https://docs.rs/struct.SharedTrieCache.html)

`SharedTrieCache`[that should be kept around per state instance requested from the backend. As there are very likely multiple accesses to the state per instance, this](https://docs.rs/struct.LocalTrieCache.html)

`LocalTrieCache`[is used to cache the nodes and the values before they are merged back to the shared instance. Last but not least there is the](https://docs.rs/struct.LocalTrieCache.html)

`LocalTrieCache`[that is being used per access to the state. It will use the](https://docs.rs/struct.TrieCache.html)

`TrieCache`[and the](https://docs.rs/struct.SharedTrieCache.html)

`SharedTrieCache`[to fulfill cache requests. If both of them don’t provide the requested data it will be inserted into the](https://docs.rs/struct.LocalTrieCache.html)

`LocalTrieCache`[and then later into the](https://docs.rs/struct.LocalTrieCache.html)

`LocalTrieCache`[.](https://docs.rs/struct.SharedTrieCache.html)

`SharedTrieCache`The [ SharedTrieCache](https://docs.rs/struct.SharedTrieCache.html) is bound to some maximum number of bytes. It is ensured that it never
runs above this limit. However as long as data is cached inside a

[it isn’t taken into account when limiting the](https://docs.rs/struct.LocalTrieCache.html)

`LocalTrieCache`[. This means that for the lifetime of a](https://docs.rs/struct.SharedTrieCache.html)

`SharedTrieCache`[the actual memory usage could be above the allowed maximum.](https://docs.rs/struct.LocalTrieCache.html)

`LocalTrieCache`## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Cache](https://docs.rs/struct.CacheSize.html)- Size
- The size of the shared cache.
- [Local](https://docs.rs/struct.LocalNodeCacheConfig.html)- Node - Cache - Config
- [Local](https://docs.rs/struct.LocalNodeCacheLimiter.html)- Node - Cache - Limiter
- [Local](https://docs.rs/struct.LocalTrieCache.html)- Trie - Cache
- The local trie cache.
- [Local](https://docs.rs/struct.LocalValueCacheConfig.html)- Value - Cache - Config
- [Local](https://docs.rs/struct.LocalValueCacheLimiter.html)- Value - Cache - Limiter
- A limiter for the local value cache. This makes sure the local cache doesn’t grow too big.
- [Shared](https://docs.rs/struct.SharedTrieCache.html)- Trie - Cache
- The shared trie cache.
- [Trie](https://docs.rs/struct.TrieCache.html)- Cache
- The actual `TrieCache`

---

# sp_trie::nibble_ops - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sp-trie/46.0.0/sp_trie/nibble_ops/index.html

## Expand description

Various re-exports from the `trie-db` crate.
Utility methods to work on radix 16 nibble.

## Constants[§](https://docs.rs#constants)

- [BIT_](https://docs.rs/constant.BIT_PER_NIBBLE.html)- PER_ - NIBBLE
- Single nibble length in bit.
- [CONTENT_](https://docs.rs/constant.CONTENT_HEADER_SIZE.html)- HEADER_ - SIZE
- Size of header.
- [NIBBLE_](https://docs.rs/constant.NIBBLE_LENGTH.html)- LENGTH
- Number of child for a branch (trie radix).
- [NIBBLE_](https://docs.rs/constant.NIBBLE_PER_BYTE.html)- PER_ - BYTE
- Number of nibble per byte.
- [PADDING_](https://docs.rs/constant.PADDING_BITMASK.html)- BITMASK
- Nibble (half a byte).
- [SPLIT_](https://docs.rs/constant.SPLIT_SHIFTS.html)- SHIFTS
- The nibble shifts needed to align. We use two value, one is a left shift and the other is a right shift.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [at](https://docs.rs/fn.at.html)
- Get u8 nibble value at a given index in a `NibbleSlice`.
- [at_left](https://docs.rs/fn.at_left.html)
- Get u8 nibble value at a given index of a byte.
- [biggest_](https://docs.rs/fn.biggest_depth.html)- depth
- Count the biggest common depth between two left aligned packed nibble slice.
- [left_](https://docs.rs/fn.left_common.html)- common
- Calculate the number of common nibble between two left aligned bytes.
- [left_](https://docs.rs/fn.left_nibble_at.html)- nibble_ - at
- Get u8 nibble value at a given index in a left aligned array.
- [number_](https://docs.rs/fn.number_padding.html)- padding
- Calculate the number of needed padding a array of nibble length `i`.
- [pad_](https://docs.rs/fn.pad_left.html)- left
- Mask a byte, keeping left nibble.
- [pad_](https://docs.rs/fn.pad_right.html)- right
- Mask a byte, keeping right byte.
- [push_](https://docs.rs/fn.push_at_left.html)- at_ - left
- Push u8 nibble value at a given index into an existing byte.
- [shift_](https://docs.rs/fn.shift_key.html)- key
- Shifts right aligned key to add a given left offset. Resulting in possibly padding at both left and right (example usage when combining two keys).

---

# sp_trie::trie_types - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sp-trie/46.0.0/sp_trie/trie_types/index.html

## Expand description

This module is for non generic definition of trie type.
Only the `Hasher` trait is generic in this case.

## Type Aliases[§](https://docs.rs#types)

- [Lookup](https://docs.rs/type.Lookup.html)
- Querying interface, as in `trie_db`but less generic.
- [TrieDB](https://docs.rs/type.TrieDB.html)
- Persistent trie database read-access interface for a given hasher.
- [TrieDB](https://docs.rs/type.TrieDBBuilder.html)- Builder
- Builder for creating a `TrieDB`
- [TrieDB](https://docs.rs/type.TrieDBMutBuilderV0.html)- MutBuilder - V0
- Builder for creating a `TrieDBMutV0`
- [TrieDB](https://docs.rs/type.TrieDBMutBuilderV1.html)- MutBuilder - V1
- Builder for creating a `TrieDBMutV1`
- [TrieDB](https://docs.rs/type.TrieDBMutV0.html)- MutV0
- Persistent trie database write-access interface for a given hasher.
- [TrieDB](https://docs.rs/type.TrieDBMutV1.html)- MutV1
- Persistent trie database write-access interface for a given hasher.
- [Trie](https://docs.rs/type.TrieError.html)- Error
- As in `trie_db`, but less generic, error type for the crate.

Look up a given hash into the bytes that hash to it, returning None if the
hash is not known.

Check for the existence of a hash-key.

Insert a datum item into the DB and return the datum’s hash for a later lookup. Insertions
are counted and the equivalent number of

`remove()`s must be performed before the data
is considered dead.## Auto Trait Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#synthetic-implementations)

# RandomState in sp_trie - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sp-trie/46.0.0/sp_trie/struct.RandomState.html

`pub struct RandomState { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

`RandomState` is the default state for [ HashMap](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/collections/hash/map/struct.HashMap.html) types.

A particular instance `RandomState` will create the same instances of
[ Hasher](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/hash/trait.Hasher.html), but the hashers created by two different

`RandomState`
instances are unlikely to produce the same result for the same values.[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::hash::RandomState;
let s = RandomState::new();
let mut map = HashMap::with_hasher(s);
map.insert(1, 2);
```
## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

# StorageProof in sp_trie - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sp-trie/46.0.0/sp_trie/struct.StorageProof.html

`pub struct StorageProof { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A proof that some set of key-value pairs are included in the storage trie. The proof contains the storage values so that the partial storage backend can be reconstructed by a verifier that does not already have access to the key-value pairs.

The proof consists of the set of serialized nodes in the storage trie accessed when looking up the keys covered by the proof. Verifying the proof requires constructing the partial trie from the serialized nodes and performing the key lookups.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<Self, [StorageProofError](https://docs.rs/enum.StorageProofError.html)>

Constructs a storage proof from a subset of encoded trie nodes in a storage backend.

Returns an error if the provided subset of encoded trie nodes contains duplicates.

Returns a new empty proof.

An empty proof is capable of only proving trivial statements (ie. that an empty set of key-value pairs exist in storage).

#### pub fn [merge](https://docs.rs#method.merge)(proofs: impl [IntoIterator](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/iter/traits/collect/trait.IntoIterator.html)<Item = Self>) -> Self

Merges multiple storage proofs covering potentially different sets of keys into one proof covering all keys. The merged proof output may be smaller than the aggregate size of the input proofs due to deduplication of trie nodes.

# MerkleValue in sp_trie - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sp-trie/46.0.0/sp_trie/enum.MerkleValue.html

## Expand description

Either the `hash` or `value` of a node depending on its size.

If the size of the node `value` is bigger or equal than `MAX_INLINE_VALUE` the `hash` is
returned.

## Variants[§](https://docs.rs#variants)

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Node)

The merkle value is the node data itself when the
node data is smaller than `MAX_INLINE_VALUE`.

Note: The case of inline nodes.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Hash)

### Hash(H)

The merkle value is the hash of the node.

    Empty,
    Leaf {
        partial:

        children: [[Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[NodeHandlePlan](https://docs.rs/trie-db/0.31.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/trie_db/node/enum.NodeHandlePlan.html)>; [16](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.array.html)],
    },
}## Expand description

Various re-exports from the `trie-db` crate.
A `NodePlan` is a blueprint for decoding a node from a byte slice. The `NodePlan` is created
by parsing an encoded node and can be reused multiple times. This is useful as a `Node` borrows
from a byte slice and this struct does not.

The enum values mirror those of `Node` except that instead of byte slices, this struct stores
ranges that can be used to index into a large byte slice.

## Variants[§](https://docs.rs#variants)

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Empty)

### Empty

Null trie node; could be an empty root or an empty branch entry.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Leaf)

### Leaf

Leaf node; has a partial key plan and value.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Extension)

### Extension

Extension node; has a partial key plan and child data.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Branch)

### Branch

Branch node; has slice of child nodes (each possibly null) and an optional immediate node data.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.NibbledBranch)

### NibbledBranch

Branch node with support for a nibble (when extension nodes are not used).

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

Build a node by decoding a byte slice according to the node plan. It is the responsibility of the caller to ensure that the node plan was created for the argument data, otherwise the call may decode incorrectly or panic.

# VerifyError in sp_trie - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sp-trie/46.0.0/sp_trie/enum.VerifyError.html

```
pub enum VerifyError<HO, CE> {
    DuplicateKey(
```
[Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)>),
    ExtraneousNode,
    ExtraneousValue([Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)>),
    ExtraneousHashReference(HO),
    InvalidChildReference([Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)>),
    ValueMismatch([Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)>),
    IncompleteProof,
    RootMismatch(HO),
    DecodeError(CE),
}## Expand description

Errors that may occur during proof verification. Most of the errors types simply indicate that the proof is invalid with respect to the statement being verified, and the exact error type can be used for debugging.

## Variants[§](https://docs.rs#variants)

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.DuplicateKey)

The statement being verified contains multiple key-value pairs with the same key. The parameter is the duplicated key.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.ExtraneousNode)

### ExtraneousNode

The proof contains at least one extraneous node.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.ExtraneousValue)

The proof contains at least one extraneous value which should have been omitted from the proof.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.ExtraneousHashReference)

### ExtraneousHashReference(HO)

The proof contains at least one extraneous hash reference the should have been omitted.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.InvalidChildReference)

The proof contains an invalid child reference that exceeds the hash length.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.ValueMismatch)

The proof indicates that an expected value was not found in the trie.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.IncompleteProof)

### IncompleteProof

The proof is missing trie nodes required to verify.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.RootMismatch)

### RootMismatch(HO)

The root hash computed from the proof is incorrect.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.DecodeError)

### DecodeError(CE)

One of the proof nodes could not be decoded.

}## Expand description

Various re-exports from the `hash-db` crate.
Trait modelling datastore keyed by a hash defined by the `Hasher`.

## Required Methods[§](https://docs.rs#required-methods)

Look up a given hash into the bytes that hash to it, returning None if the hash is not known.

Check for the existence of a hash-key.

Insert a datum item into the DB and return the datum’s hash for a later lookup. Insertions
are counted and the equivalent number of `remove()`s must be performed before the data
is considered dead.

## Trait Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#trait-implementations)

*In older versions of Rust, dyn compatibility was called "object safety".*

`is_host` is set to `true` when the transaction to rollback was started by the host.

Look up the [ MerkleValue](https://docs.rs/enum.MerkleValue.html) of the node that is the closest descendant for the provided
key.

When the provided key leads to a node, then the merkle value of that node
is returned. However, if the key does not lead to a node, then the merkle value
of the closest descendant is returned. `None` if no such descendant exists.

}## Expand description

Various re-exports from the `trie-db` crate.
A cache that can be used to speed-up certain operations when accessing the trie.

The [ TrieDB](https://docs.rs/trie-db/0.31.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/trie_db/triedb/struct.TrieDB.html)/

[by default are working with the internal hash-db in a non-owning mode. This means that for every lookup in the trie, every node is always fetched and decoded on the fly. Fetching and decoding a node always takes some time and can kill the performance of any application that is doing quite a lot of trie lookups. To circumvent this performance degradation, a cache can be used when looking up something in the trie. Any cache that should be used with the](https://docs.rs/trie-db/0.31.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/trie_db/triedbmut/struct.TrieDBMut.html)

`TrieDBMut`[/](https://docs.rs/trie-db/0.31.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/trie_db/triedb/struct.TrieDB.html)

`TrieDB`[needs to implement this trait.](https://docs.rs/trie-db/0.31.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/trie_db/triedbmut/struct.TrieDBMut.html)

`TrieDBMut`The trait is laying out a two level cache, first the trie nodes cache and then the value cache.
The trie nodes cache, as the name indicates, is for caching trie nodes as [ NodeOwned](https://docs.rs/trie-db/0.31.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/trie_db/node/enum.NodeOwned.html). These
trie nodes are referenced by their hash. The value cache is caching

[’s and these are referenced by the key to look them up in the trie. As multiple different tries can have different values under the same key, it up to the cache implementation to ensure that the correct value is returned. As each trie has a different root, this root can be used to differentiate values under the same key.](https://docs.rs/trie-db/0.31.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/trie_db/enum.CachedValue.html)

`CachedValue`## Required Methods[§](https://docs.rs#required-methods)

[Source](https://docs.rs/trie-db/0.31.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/trie_db/lib.rs.html#695)#### fn [lookup_value_for_key](https://docs.rs#tymethod.lookup_value_for_key)(
    &mut self,
    key: &[[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)],

#### fn [lookup_value_for_key](https://docs.rs#tymethod.lookup_value_for_key)(

    key: &[[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)],

Lookup value for the given `key`.

Returns the `None` if the `key` is unknown or otherwise `Some(_)` with the associated
value.

[`Self::cache_data_for_key`] is used to make the cache aware of data that is associated
to a `key`.

[§](https://docs.rs#attention)Attention

The cache can be used for different tries, aka with different roots. This means that the cache implementation needs to take care of always returning the correct value for the current trie root.

}## Expand description

Various re-exports from the `trie-db` crate.
This trait associates a trie definition with preferred methods.
It also contains own default implementations and can be
used to allow switching implementation.

## Provided Methods[§](https://docs.rs#provided-methods)

Operation to build a trie db from its ordered iterator over its key/values.

Determines a trie root given its ordered contents, closed form.

A key-value datastore implemented as a database-backed modified Merkle tree.

Remove a `key` from the trie. Equivalent to making it equal to the empty
value. Returns the old value associated with this key, if it existed.

pub trait TrieRecorder<H> {

```

}## Expand description

Various re-exports from the `trie-db` crate.
A trie recorder that can be used to record all kind of [ TrieAccess](https://docs.rs/trie-db/0.31.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/trie_db/enum.TrieAccess.html)’s.

To build a trie proof a recorder is required that records all trie accesses. These recorded trie accesses can then be used to create the proof.

Trie codec reexport, mainly child trie support for trie compact proof. Decode a compact proof.

Takes as input a destination `db` for decoded node and `encoded`
an iterator of compact encoded nodes.

Child trie are decoded in order of child trie root present in the top trie.

# encode_compact in sp_trie - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sp-trie/46.0.0/sp_trie/fn.encode_compact.html

```
pub fn encode_compact<L, DB>(
    partial_db:
```
[&DB](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.reference.html),
    root: &[TrieHash](https://docs.rs/type.TrieHash.html)<L>,
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[CompactProof](https://docs.rs/struct.CompactProof.html), [Error](https://docs.rs/enum.CompactProofError.html)<[TrieHash](https://docs.rs/type.TrieHash.html)<L>, [CError](https://docs.rs/type.CError.html)<L>>>## Expand description

Trie codec reexport, mainly child trie support for trie compact proof. Encode a compact proof.

Takes as input all full encoded node from the proof, and the root. Then parse all child trie root and compress main trie content first then all child trie contents. Child trie are ordered by the order of their roots in the top trie.

# generate_trie_proof in sp_trie - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sp-trie/46.0.0/sp_trie/fn.generate_trie_proof.html

```
pub fn generate_trie_proof<'a, L, I, K, DB>(
    db:
```
[&DB](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.reference.html),
    root: [TrieHash](https://docs.rs/type.TrieHash.html)<L>,
    keys: I,
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)>>, [Box](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/boxed/struct.Box.html)<[TrieError](https://docs.rs/type.TrieError.html)<L>>>## Expand description

Create a proof for a subset of keys in a trie.

The `keys` may contain any set of keys regardless of each one of them is included
in the `db`.

For a key `K` that is included in the `db` a proof of inclusion is generated.
For a key `K` that is not included in the `db` a proof of non-inclusion is generated.
These can be later checked in `verify_trie_proof`.

---

# verify_trie_proof in sp_trie - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sp-trie/46.0.0/sp_trie/fn.verify_trie_proof.html

```
pub fn verify_trie_proof<'a, L, I, K, V>(
    root: &
```
[TrieHash](https://docs.rs/type.TrieHash.html)<L>,
    proof: &[[Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)>],
    items: I,
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.unit.html), [VerifyError](https://docs.rs/enum.VerifyError.html)<[TrieHash](https://docs.rs/type.TrieHash.html)<L>, [CError](https://docs.rs/type.CError.html)<L>>>## Expand description

Verify a set of key-value pairs against a trie root and a proof.

Checks a set of keys with optional values for inclusion in the proof that was generated by
`generate_trie_proof`.
If the value in the pair is supplied (`(key, Some(value))`), this key-value pair will be
checked for inclusion in the proof.
If the value is omitted (`(key, None)`), this key will be checked for non-inclusion in the
proof.

---

### InvalidStateRoot(<<L as [TrieLayout](https://docs.rs/trait.TrieLayout.html)>::[Hash](https://docs.rs/trait.TrieLayout.html#associatedtype.Hash) as [Hasher](https://docs.rs/hash-db/0.16.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/hash_db/trait.Hasher.html)>::[Out](https://docs.rs/hash-db/0.16.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/hash_db/trait.Hasher.html#associatedtype.Out))

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.IncompleteDatabase)

### IncompleteDatabase(<<L as [TrieLayout](https://docs.rs/trait.TrieLayout.html)>::[Hash](https://docs.rs/trait.TrieLayout.html#associatedtype.Hash) as [Hasher](https://docs.rs/hash-db/0.16.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/hash_db/trait.Hasher.html)>::[Out](https://docs.rs/hash-db/0.16.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/hash_db/trait.Hasher.html#associatedtype.Out))

Trie item not found in the database,

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.ValueAtIncompleteKey)

A value was found in the trie with a nibble key that was not byte-aligned. The first parameter is the byte-aligned part of the prefix and the second parameter is the remaining nibble.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.DecoderError)

### DecoderError(<<L as [TrieLayout](https://docs.rs/trait.TrieLayout.html)>::[Hash](https://docs.rs/trait.TrieLayout.html#associatedtype.Hash) as [Hasher](https://docs.rs/hash-db/0.16.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/hash_db/trait.Hasher.html)>::[Out](https://docs.rs/hash-db/0.16.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/hash_db/trait.Hasher.html#associatedtype.Out), <<L as [TrieLayout](https://docs.rs/trait.TrieLayout.html)>::[Codec](https://docs.rs/trait.TrieLayout.html#associatedtype.Codec) as [NodeCodec](https://docs.rs/trie-db/0.31.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/trie_db/node_codec/trait.NodeCodec.html)>::[Error](https://docs.rs/trie-db/0.31.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/trie_db/node_codec/trait.NodeCodec.html#associatedtype.Error))

Corrupt Trie item.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.InvalidHash)

Hash is not value.

# sp_trie - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sp-trie/latest/sp_trie/

Utility functions to interact with Substrate’s Base-16 Modified Merkle Patricia tree (“trie”).

# ahash 0.8.12 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/ahash/^0.8.2

# aHash

AHash is the [fastest](https://github.com/tkaitchuck/aHash/blob/master/compare/readme.md#Speed),
[DOS resistant hash](https://github.com/tkaitchuck/aHash/wiki/How-aHash-is-resists-DOS-attacks) currently available in Rust.
AHash is intended *exclusively* for use in in-memory hashmaps.

AHash's output is of [high quality](https://github.com/tkaitchuck/aHash/blob/master/compare/readme.md#Quality) but aHash is **not** a cryptographically secure hash.

## Design

Because AHash is a keyed hash, each map will produce completely different hashes, which cannot be predicted without knowing the keys.
[This prevents DOS attacks where an attacker sends a large number of items whose hashes collide that get used as keys in a hashmap.](https://github.com/tkaitchuck/aHash/wiki/How-aHash-is-resists-DOS-attacks)

This also avoids [accidentally quadratic behavior by reading from one map and writing to another.](https://accidentallyquadratic.tumblr.com/post/153545455987/rust-hash-iteration-reinsertion)

## Goals and Non-Goals

AHash does *not* have a fixed standard for its output. This allows it to improve over time. For example,
if any faster algorithm is found, aHash will be updated to incorporate the technique.
Similarly, should any flaw in aHash's DOS resistance be found, aHash will be changed to correct the flaw.

Because it does not have a fixed standard, different computers or computers on different versions of the code will observe different hash values.
As such, aHash is not recommended for use other than in-memory maps. Specifically, aHash is not intended for network use or in applications which persist hashed values.
(In these cases `HighwayHash` would be a better choice)

Additionally, aHash is not intended to be cryptographically secure and should not be used as a MAC, or anywhere which requires a cryptographically secure hash.
(In these cases `SHA-3` would be a better choice)

## Usage

AHash is a drop in replacement for the default implementation of the `Hasher` trait. To construct a `HashMap` using aHash
as its hasher do the following:

```
use ;
use HashMap;
let mut map:  = default;
map.insert;
```
For convenience, wrappers called `AHashMap` and `AHashSet` are also provided.
These do the same thing with slightly less typing.

```
use AHashMap;
let mut map:  = new;
map.insert;
map.insert;
```
## Flags

The aHash package has the following flags:

- `std`: This enables features which require the standard library. (On by default) This includes providing the utility classes- `AHashMap`and- `AHashSet`.
- `serde`: Enables- `serde`support for the utility classes- `AHashMap`and- `AHashSet`.
- `runtime-rng`: To obtain a seed for Hashers will obtain randomness from the operating system. (On by default) This is done using the- [getrandom](https://github.com/rust-random/getrandom)crate.
- `compile-time-rng`: For OS targets without access to a random number generator,- `compile-time-rng`provides an alternative. If- `getrandom`is unavailable and- `compile-time-rng`is enabled, aHash will generate random numbers at compile time and embed them in the binary.
- `nightly-arm-aes`: To use AES instructions on 32-bit ARM, which requires nightly. This is not needed on AArch64. This allows for DOS resistance even if there is no random number generator available at runtime (assuming the compiled binary is not public). This makes the binary non-deterministic. (If non-determinism is a problem see- [constrandom's documentation](https://github.com/tkaitchuck/constrandom#deterministic-builds))

If both `runtime-rng` and `compile-time-rng` are enabled the `runtime-rng` will take precedence and `compile-time-rng` will do nothing.
If neither flag is set, seeds can be supplied by the application. [Multiple apis](https://docs.rs/ahash/latest/ahash/random_state/struct.RandomState.html)
are available to do this.

## Comparison with other hashers

A full comparison with other hashing algorithms can be found [here](https://github.com/tkaitchuck/aHash/blob/master/compare/readme.md)

For a more representative performance comparison which includes the overhead of using a HashMap, see [HashBrown's benchmarks](https://github.com/rust-lang/hashbrown#performance)
as HashBrown now uses aHash as its hasher by default.

## Hash quality

AHash passes the full [SMHasher test suite](https://github.com/rurban/smhasher).

The code to reproduce the result, and the full output [are checked into the repo](https://github.com/tkaitchuck/aHash/tree/master/smhasher).

## Additional FAQ

A separate FAQ document is maintained [here](https://github.com/tkaitchuck/aHash/blob/master/FAQ.md).
If you have questions not covered there, open an issue [here](https://github.com/tkaitchuck/aHash/issues).

## License

- Apache License, Version 2.0, ([LICENSE-APACHE](https://docs.rs/LICENSE-APACHE)or[http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0](http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0))
- MIT license ([LICENSE-MIT](https://docs.rs/LICENSE-MIT)or[http://opensource.org/licenses/MIT](http://opensource.org/licenses/MIT))

at your option.

## Contribution

Unless you explicitly state otherwise, any contribution intentionally submitted for inclusion in the work by you, as defined in the Apache-2.0 license, shall be dual licensed as above, without any additional terms or conditions.

# parity-scale-codec 3.7.5 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/parity-scale-codec/^3.7.5

# Parity SCALE Codec

Rust implementation of the SCALE (Simple Concatenated Aggregate Little-Endian) data format for types used in the Parity Substrate framework.

SCALE is a light-weight format which allows encoding (and decoding) which makes it highly suitable for resource-constrained execution environments like blockchain runtimes and low-power, low-memory devices.

It is important to note that the encoding context (knowledge of how the types and data structures look) needs to be known separately at both encoding and decoding ends. The encoded data does not include this contextual information.

To get a better understanding of how the encoding is done for different types,
take a look at the ["Type encoding (SCALE)" page in Substrate docs](https://docs.substrate.io/reference/scale-codec/).

## Implementation

The codec is implemented using the following traits:

### Encode

The `Encode` trait is used for encoding of data into the SCALE format. The `Encode` trait
contains the following functions:

- `size_hint(&self) -> usize`: Gets the capacity (in bytes) required for the encoded data. This is to avoid double-allocation of memory needed for the encoding. It can be an estimate and does not need to be an exact number. If the size is not known, even no good maximum, then we can skip this function from the trait implementation. This is required to be a cheap operation, so should not involve iterations etc.
- `encode_to<T: Output>(&self, dest: &mut T)`: Encodes the value and appends it to a destination buffer.
- `encode(&self) -> Vec<u8>`: Encodes the type data and returns a slice.
- `using_encoded<R, F: FnOnce(&[u8]) -> R>(&self, f: F) -> R`: Encodes the type data and executes a closure on the encoded value. Returns the result from the executed closure.

**Note:** Implementations should override `using_encoded` for value types and `encode_to` for
allocating types. `size_hint` should be implemented for all types, wherever possible. Wrapper
types should override all methods.

### Decode

The `Decode` trait is used for deserialization/decoding of encoded data into the respective
types.

- `fn decode<I: Input>(value: &mut I) -> Result<Self, Error>`: Tries to decode the value from SCALE format to the type it is called on. Returns an- `Err`if the decoding fails.

### CompactAs

The `CompactAs` trait is used for wrapping custom types/structs as compact types, which makes
them even more space/memory efficient. The compact encoding is described [here](https://docs.substrate.io/reference/scale-codec/#fn-1).

- `encode_as(&self) -> &Self::As`: Encodes the type (self) as a compact type. The type- `As`is defined in the same trait and its implementation should be compact encode-able.
- `decode_from(_: Self::As) -> Result<Self, Error>`: Decodes the type (self) from a compact encode-able type.

### HasCompact

The `HasCompact` trait, if implemented, tells that the corresponding type is a compact
encode-able type.

### EncodeLike

The `EncodeLike` trait needs to be implemented for each type manually. When using derive, it is
done automatically for you. Basically the trait gives you the opportunity to accept multiple
types to a function that all encode to the same representation.

## Usage Examples

Following are some examples to demonstrate usage of the codec.

### Simple types

```
# // Import macros if derive feature is not used.
#
# use ;
use ;
let a = A;
let b = B;
let c = C ;
a.using_encoded;
b.using_encoded;
c.using_encoded;
let mut da: & = b"\x0f";
assert_eq!;
let mut db: & = b"\x01\x01\0\0\0\x02\0\0\0\0\0\0\0";
assert_eq!;
let mut dc: & = b"\x02\x01\0\0\0\x02\0\0\0\0\0\0\0";
assert_eq!;
let mut dz: & = &;
assert_eq!;
#
```
### Compact type with HasCompact

```
# // Import macros if derive feature is not used.
#
# use ;
use ;
let test_val:  = ;
let encoded = Test1HasCompact .encode;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
#
```
### Type with CompactAs

```
# // Import macros if derive feature is not used.
#
# use ;
use ;
use ;
;
let a =  ;
let encoded = a.encode;
assert_eq!;
#
```
## Derive attributes

The derive implementation supports the following attributes:

- `codec(dumb_trait_bound)`: This attribute needs to be placed above the type that one of the trait should be implemented for. It will make the algorithm that determines the to-add trait bounds fall back to just use the type parameters of the type. This can be useful for situation where the algorithm includes private types in the public interface. By using this attribute, you should not get this error/warning again.
- `codec(skip)`: Needs to be placed above a field or variant and makes it to be skipped while encoding/decoding.
- `codec(compact)`: Needs to be placed above a field and makes the field use compact encoding. (The type needs to support compact encoding.)
- `codec(encoded_as = "OtherType")`: Needs to be placed above a field and makes the field being encoded by using- `OtherType`.
- `codec(index = 0)`: Needs to be placed above an enum variant to make the variant use the given index when encoded. By default the index is determined by counting from- `0`beginning wth the first variant.
- `codec(encode_bound)`,- `codec(decode_bound)`and- `codec(mel_bound)`: All 3 attributes take in a- `where`clause for the- `Encode`,- `Decode`and- `MaxEncodedLen`trait implementation for the annotated type respectively.
- `codec(encode_bound(skip_type_params))`,- `codec(decode_bound(skip_type_params))`and- `codec(mel_bound(skip_type_params))`: All 3 sub-attributes take in types as arguments to skip trait derivation of the corresponding trait, e.g. T in- `codec(encode_bound(skip_type_params(T)))`will not contain a- `Encode`trait bound while- `Encode`is being derived for the annotated type.

## Known issues

Even though this crate supports deserialization of arbitrarily sized array (e.g. `[T; 1024 * 1024 * 1024]`)
using such types is not recommended and will most likely result in a stack overflow. If you have a big
array inside of your structure which you want to decode you should wrap it in a `Box`, e.g. `Box<[T; 1024 * 1024 * 1024]>`.

License: Apache-2.0

---

# foldhash 0.1.5 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/foldhash/^0.1.5

# Foldhash

This repository contains foldhash, a fast, non-cryptographic, minimally DoS-resistant hashing algorithm implemented in Rust designed for computational uses such as hash maps, bloom filters, count sketching, etc.

When should you **not** use foldhash:

-
You are afraid of people studying your long-running program's behavior to reverse engineer its internal random state and using this knowledge to create many colliding inputs for computational complexity attacks. For more details see the section "HashDoS resistance".
-
You expect foldhash to have a consistent output across versions or platforms, such as for persistent file formats or communication protocols.
-
You are relying on foldhash's properties for any kind of security. Foldhash is **not appropriate for any cryptographic purpose**.

Foldhash has two variants, one optimized for speed which is ideal for data
structures such as hash maps and bloom filters, and one optimized for
statistical quality which is ideal for algorithms such as
[HyperLogLog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HyperLogLog) and
[MinHash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MinHash).

Foldhash can be used in a `#![no_std]` environment by disabling its default
`"std"` feature.

## Performance

We evaluated foldhash against three commonly used hashes in Rust:
[aHash](https://github.com/tkaitchuck/aHash) v0.8.11,
[fxhash](https://github.com/cbreeden/fxhash) v0.2.1, and
[SipHash-1-3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SipHash), the default hash algorithm
in Rust at the time of writing. We evaluated both variants foldhash provides,
`foldhash-f` and `foldhash-q`, which correspond to `foldhash::fast` and
`foldhash::quality` in the crate respectively.

First we note that hashers with random state inflate the size of your `HashMap`,
which may or may not be important for your performance:

```
 = 40  // (both variants)
 = 64
 = 32
 = 48
```
We tested runtime performance on two machines, one with a 2023 Apple M2 CPU, one
with a 2023 Intel Xeon Platinum 8481C server CPU, both with stable Rust 1.80.1.
Since one of our competitors (aHash) is reliant on AES-based instructions for
optimal performance we have included both a benchmark with and without
`-C target-cpu=native` for the Intel machine.

We tested across a wide variety of data types we consider representative of types / distributions one might hash in the real world, in the context of a hash table key:

- `u32`- random 32-bit unsigned integers,
- `u32pair`- pairs of random 32-bit unsigned integers,
- `u64`- random 64-bit unsigned integers,
- `u64pair`- pairs of random 64-bit unsigned integers,
- `u64lobits`- 64-bit unsigned integers where only the bottom 16 bits vary,
- `u64hibits`- 64-bit unsigned integers where only the top 16 bits vary,
- `ipv4`-- `std::net::Ipv4Addr`- `[u8; 4]`,
- `ipv6`-- `std::net::Ipv6Addr`- `[u8; 16]`,
- `rgba`- random- `(u8, u8, u8, u8)`tuples,
- `strenglishword`- strings containing words sampled uniformly from the top 10,000 most common English words,
- `struuid`- random UUIDs, hashed in string representation,
- `strurl`- strings containing URLs sampled uniformly from a corpus of 10,000 URLs,
- `strdate`- random- `YYYY-MM-DD`date strings,
- `accesslog`-- `(u128, u32, chrono::NaiveDate, bool)`, meant to simulate a typical larger compound type, in this case- `(resource_id, user_id, date, success)`for an access log.
- `kilobyte`- random bytestrings one kilobyte in length,
- `tenkilobyte`- random bytestrings ten kilobytes in length.

We tested the performance of hashing the above data types in the following four contexts:

- `hashonly`- only the time it takes to hash the value,
- `lookupmiss`- the time it takes to do a lookup in a 1,000 element hash map of random elements, only sampling keys of which we know that are not in the hash map,
- `lookuphit`- similar to- `lookupmiss`, except the keys are sampled from keys known to be in the hash map,
- `setbuild`- the time it takes to construct a- `HashSet`of 1,000 elements from 1,000 randomly sampled elements each repeated 10 times (so 10,000 inserts, with ~90% duplicates).

All times are reported as expected time per operation, so one hash, one lookup,
or one insert respectively. The full results [can be found
here](https://gist.github.com/orlp/1271ad5b8b775c651cc55773888858eb). To
summarize, we will only show the results for `u64` and `strenglishword` here, as
well as the observed geometric mean and average rank over the full benchmark.

```
